hens_rule_text: One chicken (or duck or rabbit) per 800 square feet of lot area, which is 6 on a standard 4,800 square foot lot. A license from the Department of Public Health is required.
permit_notes: A two-year farm animal license from the Cleveland Department of Public Health is required (Sec. 205.04). The application asks for a scaled site drawing, a coop description, a waste removal plan, and owner permission if you rent.
setback_notes: Coops may not be in front or side street yards, and must be at least 5 feet from a side lot line and 18 inches from a rear lot line (5 feet if that rear line borders the side or front of a neighboring lot).
coop_rules: Covered, predator-proof, ventilated coop; total coop area no more than 32 sq ft for up to 6 animals and no taller than 15 ft; a fenced outdoor run with at least 10 sq ft per bird.
zoning_notes: In non-residential districts the limit is one animal per 400 sq ft. Roosters, geese and turkeys are banned in residential districts unless the parcel is at least 1 acre and the coop is 100 feet from all property lines.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
